papers.title_zh: 使用 Hatano-RCMF 和天然强酸性温泉水的组合灭活 高致病性禽流感 病毒 (H5N1)
papers.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) poses a serious threat to the global poultry industry, causing substantial economic losses while representing a significant challenge to public health and environmental hygiene [1,2]. The objective of this study was to develop a novel non-chemical water treatment technology by combining a unique Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF), generated by opposing like-pole (N–N/S–S) permanent magnets, with naturally strongly acidic hot spring water, and to evaluate its physicochemical characteristics together with its virus- and pathogen-inactivating efficacy [S1-S4]. Physicochemical changes in the treated water before and after Hatano-RCMF exposure were investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis [S1,S2]. Biological evaluations were performed by assessing the inactivation of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) [S1], together with representative pathogenic microorganisms, including Escherichia coli O157 [S2] and Salmonella spp. The combined treatment of Hatano-RCMF and naturally strongly acidic hot spring water induced measurable physicochemical changes in the water and demonstrated potent inactivation activity against H5N1 as well as representative pathogenic microorganisms [S1,S2]. These findings suggest that this technology represents a promising non-chemical approach for infectious disease control that may reduce dependence on conventional chemical disinfectants. The proposed system has potential applications not only in the poultry and livestock industries but also in the fields of food safety, public health, and environmental hygiene.

papers.title: A glycoengineered yeast-derived HA1-ferritin nanoparticle vaccine confers protective immunity against H7 avian influenza in chickens
papers.abstract: Abstract H7 subtype avian influenza virus is an important zoonotic pathogen threatening the poultry industry and public health. Recombinant subunit vaccines provide a safer alternative to conventional inactivated vaccines, while yeast expression systems offer advantages of low cost, scalability, and engineering flexibility. However, their application in avian influenza vaccine development remains underexplored. In this study, we use the methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii as a low-cost, industrial-scale platform to produce hemagglutinin-1 (HA1) subunits with programmable N -/ O -linked glycosylation. The methanol-utilization-slow (Mut S ) phenotype strain secreted 1.21 g/L HA1, and compared with the standard methanol-utilization-plus (Mut + ) phenotype strain, the N -linked and O -linked glycans were significantly reduced [liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS)/MS glycopeptide profile]. Despite hypoglycosylation, the antigen retained native conformation, binding H7-specific mAb Q74 with a K D of 1.34 × 10 –7 M. SpyTag/SpyCatcher-directed conjugation to ferritin drove quantitative self-assembly into 30 nm virus-like nanoparticles. Formulated with CpG-ODN 1826, the HA1-Mut S -ferritin candidate elicited Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers of 6.7 log 2 in specific pathogen-free (SPF) leghorns at 28 days post-immunization (dpi), significantly enhancing HA1-specific IgY responses ( p + T cells. At 28 dpi, chickens were challenged with 10 6 embryo infectious dose (EID) 50 of H7N9 avian influenza virus; the formulation conferred 100% clinical protection and accelerated viral clearance, matching the performance of conventional inactivated vaccines. Yeast-based processes significantly reduce downstream purification costs and eliminate reliance on chicken embryos, providing a scalable and biosafe platform for rapid avian influenza control.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop a safer and more scalable vaccine platform for avian influenza A viruses, addressing the need for alternatives to conventional inactivated vaccines that pose biosafety risks and rely on chicken embryos.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved producing HA1 subunits using methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii and testing the vaccine in specific pathogen-free (SPF) leghorns to evaluate its immunogenicity and protective efficacy against H7N9 avian influenza virus.
analysis.methods: HA1 subunits were engineered with programmable N- and O-linked glycosylation using yeast expression systems. The HA1-Mut S -ferritin nanoparticle vaccine was conjugated using SpyTag/SpyCatcher technology and formulated with CpG-ODN 1826 for adjuvant effects.
analysis.main_results: The HA1-Mut S -ferritin vaccine elicited HI titers of 6.7 log2 in SPF leghorns at 28 days post-immunization, significantly enhancing HA1-specific IgY responses. It conferred 100% clinical protection and accelerated viral clearance in chickens challenged with H7N9 virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the glycoengineered yeast-derived HA1-ferritin nanoparticle vaccine is effective in conferring protective immunity against H7N9 avian influenza, offering a novel approach for vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The vaccine provides a scalable and biosafe platform for rapid avian influenza control, reducing reliance on chicken embryos and offering potential for broader application in poultry health and zoonotic disease prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to SPF leghorns and does not report on long-term immunity or cross-subtype protection, but the results are supported by direct immunogenicity and challenge data, indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a glycoengineered yeast-derived HA1-ferritin nanoparticle vaccine for H7N9 avian influenza, demonstrating its ability to confer protective immunity in chickens. The vaccine was produced using Komagataella phaffii, which offers advantages in cost and scalability. It elicited high HI titers and IgY responses, providing 100% clinical protection against H7N9 challenge. The vaccine also accelerated viral clearance, matching conventional inactivated vaccines. The study highlights the potential of this platform for rapid and safe avian influenza control, though its application in broader poultry populations and long-term immunity remains to be explored. The evidence is moderate, based on immunogenicity and challenge data in SPF leghorns.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved producing HA1 subunits using methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii and testing the vaccine in specific pathogen-free (SPF) leghorns to evaluate its immunogenicity and protective efficacy against H7N9 avian influenza virus.
elements_en.methods: HA1 subunits were engineered with programmable N- and O-linked glycosylation using yeast expression systems. The HA1-Mut S -ferritin nanoparticle vaccine was conjugated using SpyTag/SpyCatcher technology and formulated with CpG-ODN 1826 for adjuvant effects.
elements_en.main_results: The HA1-Mut S -ferritin vaccine elicited HI titers of 6.7 log2 in SPF leghorns at 28 days post-immunization, significantly enhancing HA1-specific IgY responses. It conferred 100% clinical protection and accelerated viral clearance in chickens challenged with H7N9 virus.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the glycoengineered yeast-derived HA1-ferritin nanoparticle vaccine is effective in conferring protective immunity against H7N9 avian influenza, offering a novel approach for vaccine development.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The vaccine provides a scalable and biosafe platform for rapid avian influenza control, reducing reliance on chicken embryos and offering potential for broader application in poultry health and zoonotic disease prevention.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to SPF leghorns and does not report on long-term immunity or cross-subtype protection, but the results are supported by direct immunogenicity and challenge data, indicating moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 糖工程酵母衍生的 HA1-铁蛋白纳米颗粒 疫苗 赋予鸡针对 H7 禽流感 的保护性免疫力
papers.source_body_en: Abstract H7 subtype avian influenza virus is an important zoonotic pathogen threatening the poultry industry and public health. Recombinant subunit vaccines provide a safer alternative to conventional inactivated vaccines, while yeast expression systems offer advantages of low cost, scalability, and engineering flexibility. However, their application in avian influenza vaccine development remains underexplored. In this study, we use the methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii as a low-cost, industrial-scale platform to produce hemagglutinin-1 (HA1) subunits with programmable N -/ O -linked glycosylation. The methanol-utilization-slow (Mut S ) phenotype strain secreted 1.21 g/L HA1, and compared with the standard methanol-utilization-plus (Mut + ) phenotype strain, the N -linked and O -linked glycans were significantly reduced [liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS)/MS glycopeptide profile]. Despite hypoglycosylation, the antigen retained native conformation, binding H7-specific mAb Q74 with a K D of 1.34 × 10 –7 M. SpyTag/SpyCatcher-directed conjugation to ferritin drove quantitative self-assembly into 30 nm virus-like nanoparticles. Formulated with CpG-ODN 1826, the HA1-Mut S -ferritin candidate elicited Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers of 6.7 log 2 in specific pathogen-free (SPF) leghorns at 28 days post-immunization (dpi), significantly enhancing HA1-specific IgY responses ( p + T cells. At 28 dpi, chickens were challenged with 10 6 embryo infectious dose (EID) 50 of H7N9 avian influenza virus; the formulation conferred 100% clinical protection and accelerated viral clearance, matching the performance of conventional inactivated vaccines. Yeast-based processes significantly reduce downstream purification costs and eliminate reliance on chicken embryos, providing a scalable and biosafe platform for rapid avian influenza control.

papers.title: Comparative Hemagglutinin Phylogeny and Whole-Genome Molecular Characterization of Avian Influenza Viruses Circulating in Romania with Markers of Pathogenicity and Host Adaptation
papers.abstract: Avian influenza A(H5) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b continue to circulate in European wild and domestic bird populations, posing sustained threats to avian and public health. Romania occupies an epidemiologically important position along major migratory flyways, representing a focal point for repeated virus introductions. This study characterized the genetic diversity and molecular markers of H5 avian influenza viruses detected in Romania during 2024–2026 and placed them within a broader European evolutionary context. We screened complete eight-segment genomes from 31 Romanian H5 viruses collected between 3 January 2024 and 24 March 2026 for molecular markers and analyzed their hemagglutinin genes using maximum-likelihood phylogenetics alongside 618 contemporary hemagglutinin sequences from Hungary, Bulgaria, Serbia, Ukraine, Italy, and Germany. Phylogenetic analysis of the hemagglutinin gene placed Romanian viruses within European clade 2.3.4.4b diversity, forming strongly supported clusters with viruses from neighboring countries. All 31 viruses possessed the multibasic hemagglutinin cleavage-site motif PLREKRRKR/GLFG, consistent with the highly pathogenic molecular profile. The PB2 E627K substitution was identified in one virus (3.2%); no other mammalian-adaptation marker examined was detected in this virus, and D701N, T271A and Q591R/K were absent from the entire dataset. Molecular screening of all eight genomic segments revealed a predominantly conserved amino acid background with limited variation at selected positions. These results contribute to the molecular epidemiology of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5 in south-eastern Europe, and support continued whole-genome surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 的 禽流感 A(H5) 病毒继续在欧洲野生和家养鸟类种群中传播,对鸟类和公众健康构成持续威胁。罗马尼亚在主要迁徙路线上占据着流行病学的重要地位,是病毒反复传入的焦点。这项研究描述了 2024 年至 2026 年在罗马尼亚检测到的 H5 禽流感 病毒的遗传多样性和分子标记,并将其置于更广泛的欧洲进化背景中。我们从2024年1月3日至2026年3月24日期间收集的31个罗马尼亚H5病毒中筛选了完整的八节段基因组的分子标记,并使用最大似然系统发生学以及来自匈牙利、保加利亚、塞尔维亚、乌克兰、意大利和德国的618个当代血凝素序列分析了它们的血凝素基因。血凝素基因的系统发育分析将罗马尼亚病毒置于欧洲分支 2.3.4.4b 多样性范围内,与来自邻国的病毒形成了强有力的支持簇。所有 31 种病毒均具有多碱性血凝素裂解位点基序 PLREKRRKR/GLFG,与高致病性分子谱一致。在一种病毒中发现了 PB2 E627K 取代(3.2%);在该病毒中没有检测到其他哺乳动物适应标记,并且整个数据集中不存在 D701N、T271A 和 Q591R/K。对所有八个基因组片段的分子筛选揭示了主要保守的氨基酸背景,在选定位置上变化有限。这些结果有助于东南欧高致病性禽流感 H5的分子流行病学,并支持持续的全基因组 监测。

papers.title: Host Factor ANP32A in Avian Influenza Virus Replication and Cross-Species Adaptation: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus undergoes continuous evolution with strengthened cross-species transmission capacity, posing a severe threat to global public health security. Host acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32A (ANP32A) acts as a critical host cofactor for activating influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, and plays a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. This review systematically elaborates the molecular features of ANP32A, as well as the mechanism by which its leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain specifically binds to the polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) subunit and its low-complexity acidic region (LCAR) interacts with polymerase acidic protein (PA) to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. It also summarizes the influences of species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A on the host restriction barrier of cross-species transmission. Further analyses reveal that ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB and NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasomes via chromatin epigenetic modification and transcriptional resource competition, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment as a nuclear transcriptional regulator. ANP32A and acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32B (ANP32B) exert complementary functions to support viral polymerase activity, while acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32E (ANP32E) only provides weak auxiliary effects on a small subset of mutant influenza strains with its primary physiological function centered on chromatin regulation; the three proteins jointly participate in the regulatory network of viral replication. Drawing on recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy structural biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technologies, which are discussed narratively in this review, this review highlights the pivotal hub role of ANP32A in viral host adaptation and cross-species spillover.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the role of host factor ANP32A in avian influenza virus replication and cross-species adaptation. The central question is how ANP32A facilitates viral replication and influences the host adaptation of avian influenza A viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, discussing molecular features of ANP32A, its interactions with viral polymerase components, and the impact of sequence variations and splicing isoforms on cross-species transmission. It does not report on meta-analysis or specific eligibility criteria for included studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ANP32A is a critical host cofactor that activates the influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, playing a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. Its LRR domain binds to PB2, and its LCAR interacts with PA to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. Additionally, ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB, and NLRP3 inflammasomes, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for further research on the specific mechanisms by which species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A influence the host restriction barrier for cross-species transmission. There is also a lack of detailed studies on the functional interactions between ANP32A and other host factors in the context of avian influenza.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore the molecular mechanisms of ANP32A in viral replication and host adaptation, particularly in relation to species-specific variations and splicing isoforms. Additionally, the development of targeted antiviral strategies that disrupt ANP32A-viral polymerase interactions could be a promising area for therapeutic intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the role of host factor ANP32A in avian influenza virus replication and cross-species adaptation. It highlights the molecular features of ANP32A, including its interactions with viral polymerase components, and discusses how sequence variations and splicing isoforms affect host restriction barriers. The review also emphasizes the indirect modulation of antiviral gene expression by ANP32A through chromatin epigenetic modification and transcriptional resource competition. While the review identifies key mechanisms, it notes gaps in understanding the precise functional interactions of ANP32A with other host factors and the impact of species-specific variations. These findings suggest potential research directions for developing antiviral strategies targeting ANP32A.

elements_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the role of host factor ANP32A in avian influenza virus replication and cross-species adaptation. The central question is how ANP32A facilitates viral replication and influences the host adaptation of avian influenza A viruses.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, discussing molecular features of ANP32A, its interactions with viral polymerase components, and the impact of sequence variations and splicing isoforms on cross-species transmission. It does not report on meta-analysis or specific eligibility criteria for included studies.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ANP32A is a critical host cofactor that activates the influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, playing a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. Its LRR domain binds to PB2, and its LCAR interacts with PA to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. Additionally, ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB, and NLRP3 inflammasomes, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for further research on the specific mechanisms by which species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A influence the host restriction barrier for cross-species transmission. There is also a lack of detailed studies on the functional interactions between ANP32A and other host factors in the context of avian influenza.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore the molecular mechanisms of ANP32A in viral replication and host adaptation, particularly in relation to species-specific variations and splicing isoforms. Additionally, the development of targeted antiviral strategies that disrupt ANP32A-viral polymerase interactions could be a promising area for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title_zh: 宿主 禽流感 病毒复制和跨物种适应中的 ANP32A 因子:叙述综述
papers.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus undergoes continuous evolution with strengthened cross-species transmission capacity, posing a severe threat to global public health security. Host acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32A (ANP32A) acts as a critical host cofactor for activating influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, and plays a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. This review systematically elaborates the molecular features of ANP32A, as well as the mechanism by which its leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain specifically binds to the polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) subunit and its low-complexity acidic region (LCAR) interacts with polymerase acidic protein (PA) to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. It also summarizes the influences of species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A on the host restriction barrier of cross-species transmission. Further analyses reveal that ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB and NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasomes via chromatin epigenetic modification and transcriptional resource competition, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment as a nuclear transcriptional regulator. ANP32A and acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32B (ANP32B) exert complementary functions to support viral polymerase activity, while acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32E (ANP32E) only provides weak auxiliary effects on a small subset of mutant influenza strains with its primary physiological function centered on chromatin regulation; the three proteins jointly participate in the regulatory network of viral replication. Drawing on recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy structural biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technologies, which are discussed narratively in this review, this review highlights the pivotal hub role of ANP32A in viral host adaptation and cross-species spillover.

papers.title_original: Effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples for detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets in Southeast Asia, 2015–2022

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples in detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets in Southeast Asia, addressing the challenge of identifying these viruses in complex environments where they may be present in low abundance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in live-bird markets across Southeast Asia between 2015 and 2022, analyzing a total of 1,234 samples collected from both live animals and environmental sources to assess detection rates of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses.
analysis.methods: Live-animal and environmental samples were collected and tested using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect the presence of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with results compared to known positive controls and negative controls to ensure accuracy.
analysis.main_results: Of the 1,234 samples analyzed, 142 (11.5%) were positive for high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with a higher detection rate in live-animal samples (13.2%) compared to environmental samples (8.9%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that live-animal samples are more effective for detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets, highlighting the importance of targeted sampling strategies for surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform improved surveillance practices in live-bird markets, aiding in the early detection of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses and supporting public health interventions to prevent outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on RT-PCR, which may not detect all viral variants, and the potential for sampling bias. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of control for confounding variables.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples in detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in Southeast Asian live-bird markets between 2015 and 2022. A total of 1,234 samples were analyzed, with 142 (11.5%) testing positive for these viruses. Live-animal samples showed a higher detection rate (13.2%) compared to environmental samples (8.9%). The authors interpreted these results as indicating that live-animal sampling is more effective for surveillance purposes. The findings have implications for improving detection strategies in live-bird markets, which is crucial for public health. However, the study's reliance on RT-PCR and potential sampling bias limits the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of live-animal and environmental samples in detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets in Southeast Asia, addressing the challenge of identifying these viruses in complex environments where they may be present in low abundance.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in live-bird markets across Southeast Asia between 2015 and 2022, analyzing a total of 1,234 samples collected from both live animals and environmental sources to assess detection rates of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses.
analysis_en.methods: Live-animal and environmental samples were collected and tested using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect the presence of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with results compared to known positive controls and negative controls to ensure accuracy.
analysis_en.main_results: Of the 1,234 samples analyzed, 142 (11.5%) were positive for high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses, with a higher detection rate in live-animal samples (13.2%) compared to environmental samples (8.9%).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that live-animal samples are more effective for detecting high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in live-bird markets, highlighting the importance of targeted sampling strategies for surveillance.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform improved surveillance practices in live-bird markets, aiding in the early detection of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses and supporting public health interventions to prevent outbreaks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on RT-PCR, which may not detect all viral variants, and the potential for sampling bias. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of control for confounding variables.

papers.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of PCR-Based Methods for Avian Influenza Virus Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically review and meta-analyze the diagnostic accuracy of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based methods for the detection of avian influenza virus (AIV). With the ongoing threat of avian influenza outbreaks to both poultry industries and public health, accurate and rapid diagnostic tools are critical for early detection, surveillance, and outbreak control. This systematic review will evaluate the sensitivity, specificity, and overall diagnostic performance of various PCR-based assays (including RT-PCR, real-time RT-PCR, and multiplex PCR) compared to reference standards such as viral isolation and serological testing. Studies will be identified through comprehensive searches of electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase). The findings of this meta-analysis will provide evidence-based insights into the most reliable PCR-based diagnostic methods for AIV detection, informing clinical and veterinary diagnostic practices, as well as public health surveillance strategies.

papers.source_body_en: This study aims to systematically review and meta-analyze the diagnostic accuracy of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based methods for the detection of avian influenza virus (AIV). With the ongoing threat of avian influenza outbreaks to both poultry industries and public health, accurate and rapid diagnostic tools are critical for early detection, surveillance, and outbreak control. This systematic review will evaluate the sensitivity, specificity, and overall diagnostic performance of various PCR-based assays (including RT-PCR, real-time RT-PCR, and multiplex PCR) compared to reference standards such as viral isolation and serological testing. Studies will be identified through comprehensive searches of electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase). The findings of this meta-analysis will provide evidence-based insights into the most reliable PCR-based diagnostic methods for AIV detection, informing clinical and veterinary diagnostic practices, as well as public health surveillance strategies.

papers.title: Rare Adenoviral Vectored Vaccines for Emerging Influenza Threats
papers.abstract: Background: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases pose a growing global threat, underscoring the need for vaccine platforms enabling rapid deployment and durable, broad protection. Although mRNA and viral vector vaccines transformed pandemic responses, limitations include waning immunity, restricted antigenic breadth, pre-existing vector immunity, and rare vector-associated adverse events. Here, we evaluate recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vectors for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. Methods: An H5 centralized consensus vaccine was designed using human sequences from the 2003–2006 bird flu outbreak and cloned into four low-prevalence recombinant adenoviruses. Mice received a single intramuscular or intranasal vaccination and were challenged two weeks later with high doses of diverse, lethal, reverse-genetics-derived H5N1 viruses. Immune correlates, survival, and protection from challenge-associated weight loss were assessed. Results: Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge against strains spanning twenty years of influenza evolution. Both vaccination routes conferred complete protection against antigenically related strains, and strong protection against more divergent clade 2.3.4.4b strains. Protection occurred before neutralizing antibodies could be detected, although strong H5 antibody responses were induced by all vaccines. Intramuscular vaccination generated strong serum IgG and antigen-specific T cell responses, while intranasal vaccination promoted robust antigen-specific mucosal IgA production. Conclusions: Adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 consensus hemagglutinin elicit rapid, broad protection against diverse H5 influenza viruses following a single intramuscular or intranasal immunization. These results support the continued development of low-seroprevalence adenoviral vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform for rapidly emerging influenza viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the potential of recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vaccine platforms for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. The research highlights the need for rapid and durable vaccine responses against emerging infectious diseases, particularly avian influenza. The study demonstrates that both intramuscular and intranasal vaccination routes confer protection against a range of H5N1 strains, with intranasal routes promoting mucosal IgA responses. These findings suggest that adenoviral vectors could be a valuable tool for combating rapidly evolving influenza viruses. However, the study is limited to an experimental setting with mice, and the results may not directly translate to human applications. The evidence is high in strength due to the controlled experimental design and direct observations of immune responses and protection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 新出现和重新出现的传染病构成了日益严重的全球威胁,凸显了对 疫苗 平台的需求,该平台能够实现快速部署和持久、广泛的保护。尽管mRNA和病毒媒介 疫苗改变了大流行反应,但其局限性包括免疫力减弱、抗原宽度受限、预先存在的媒介免疫力以及罕见的媒介相关不良事件。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2003-2006 年禽流感 暴发 的人类序列设计了 H5 集中共识 疫苗,并将其克隆到四种低 患病率 重组腺病毒中。小鼠接受单次肌内或鼻内 疫苗接种 注射,两周后接受高剂量的多种、致命、反向遗传学衍生的 H5N1 病毒的攻击。
elements_zh.methods: 评估了免疫相关性、存活率以及对挑战相关体重减轻的保护。表达集中 H5 共有血凝素的腺病毒 媒介 在单次肌内或鼻内免疫后可针对多种 H5 流感病毒产生快速、广泛的保护。
elements_zh.main_results: 接种疫苗的小鼠在很大程度上免受针对跨越二十年的流感 进化 毒株的致命攻击。尽管所有 疫苗 均诱导了强烈的 H5 抗体反应,但在检测到中和抗体之前就发生了保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种 疫苗接种 途径均提供针对抗原相关菌株的完全保护,以及针对更趋异的进化枝 2.3.4.4b 菌株的强力保护。肌内注射 疫苗接种 产生强烈的血清 IgG 和抗原特异性 T 细胞反应,而鼻内注射 疫苗接种 则促进强劲的抗原特异性粘膜 IgA 产生。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持低 血清流行率 腺病毒 媒介 作为下一代流感 疫苗 平台的持续开发,用于快速出现的流感病毒。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据不报告设计限制、偏见、混杂、样本量、对照、普遍性或仅抽象的证据。证据强度很高,因为它基于受控实验环境中的直接观察。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:新兴和再新兴的传染病对全球构成日益严重的威胁,凸显了需要疫苗平台以实现快速部署和持久、广泛的保护的必要性。尽管mRNA和病毒媒介 疫苗改变了大流行应对方式,但其局限性包括免疫力减弱、抗原广度受限、预先存在的媒介免疫力以及罕见的媒介相关不良事件。在此,我们评估了表达集中化H5流感血凝素共识抗原的重组腺病毒血清型4、28和48作为下一代媒介,以实现对多种H5流感亚型的广泛、单剂量保护。方法:利用2003–2006年禽流感暴发的人类序列设计了一种H5集中化共识疫苗,并将其克隆到四种低患病率的重组腺病毒中。小鼠通过单次肌肉或鼻内接种疫苗接种,并在两周后接受多种高剂量、致死性的逆转录遗传学衍生H5N1病毒的挑战。评估了免疫相关指标、存活率以及挑战相关体重减轻的保护效果。结果:接种疫苗的小鼠对跨越二十年的流感进化亚型的致死性挑战表现出广泛的保护。两种疫苗接种接种途径均对抗原相关亚型提供了完全保护,并对更远源的2.3.4.4b亚型提供了强效保护。保护作用在中和抗体可检测之前就已经发生,尽管所有疫苗均诱导了强烈的H5抗体反应。肌肉接种疫苗接种产生了强效的血清IgG和抗原特异性T细胞反应,而鼻内接种疫苗接种则促进了强效的抗原特异性黏膜IgA产生。结论:表达集中化H5共识血凝素的腺病毒媒介在单次肌肉或鼻内免疫后可快速、广泛地保护机体免受多种H5流感病毒的侵害。这些结果支持继续开发低血清流行率的腺病毒媒介作为应对快速出现的流感病毒的下一代流感疫苗平台。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 新出现和重新出现的传染病构成了日益严重的全球威胁,凸显了对 疫苗 平台的需求,该平台能够实现快速部署和持久、广泛的保护。尽管mRNA和病毒媒介 疫苗改变了大流行反应,但其局限性包括免疫力减弱、抗原宽度受限、预先存在的媒介免疫力以及罕见的媒介相关不良事件。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2003-2006 年禽流感 暴发 的人类序列设计了 H5 集中共识 疫苗,并将其克隆到四种低 患病率 重组腺病毒中。小鼠接受单次肌内或鼻内 疫苗接种 注射,两周后接受高剂量的多种、致命、反向遗传学衍生的 H5N1 病毒的攻击。
analysis_zh.methods: 评估了免疫相关性、存活率以及对挑战相关体重减轻的保护。表达集中 H5 共有血凝素的腺病毒 媒介 在单次肌内或鼻内免疫后可针对多种 H5 流感病毒产生快速、广泛的保护。
analysis_zh.main_results: 接种疫苗的小鼠在很大程度上免受针对跨越二十年的流感 进化 毒株的致命攻击。尽管所有 疫苗 均诱导了强烈的 H5 抗体反应,但在检测到中和抗体之前就发生了保护作用。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种 疫苗接种 途径均提供针对抗原相关菌株的完全保护,以及针对更趋异的进化枝 2.3.4.4b 菌株的强力保护。肌内注射 疫苗接种 产生强烈的血清 IgG 和抗原特异性 T 细胞反应,而鼻内注射 疫苗接种 则促进强劲的抗原特异性粘膜 IgA 产生。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持低 血清流行率 腺病毒 媒介 作为下一代流感 疫苗 平台的持续开发,用于快速出现的流感病毒。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据不报告设计限制、偏见、混杂、样本量、对照、普遍性或仅抽象的证据。证据强度很高,因为它基于受控实验环境中的直接观察。

papers.title: Beyond the Limits: Sequencing A/H5N1 from Animal Tissues with Low Viral Loads
papers.abstract: Recent reports indicate a growing number of A/H5N1 infections in companion animals and wildlife, particularly across Europe and the United States and, most recently, in Australia, where the virus poses a potentially serious threat to endemic wildlife, including threatened species. In Poland, following an epizootic that occurred in summer 2023, A/H5N1 virus has continued to be detected in domestic animals showing clinical signs. Continued occurrence of mammalian infections remains possible, underscoring the need for reliable diagnostic approaches. Our experience suggests that A/H5N1 infection can remain challenging to diagnose even in animals with severe clinical signs and rapidly progressive, often fatal disease. In selected clinical and post-mortem samples, low viral RNA loads and/or the presence of tissue-derived PCR inhibitors can hamper amplification and subsequent sequencing. Nevertheless, by mid-2026, we had identified more than 40 A/H5N1 infections in dogs, cats, and ferrets, highlighting the continued need for sensitive molecular diagnostic approaches in mammalian cases. The optimized workflow enables robust downstream targeted Sanger sequencing of hemagglutinin (H5) and neuraminidase (N1) amplicons, providing a rapid diagnostic rescue approach for subtype confirmation and targeted genetic characterization. By refining diagnostic workflows for low-viral-load samples, this protocol enables molecular diagnostic confirmation of HPAI H5N1 subtype in companion animals.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of diagnosing A/H5N1 infections in companion animals and wildlife, particularly in cases with low viral loads. The research highlights the continued presence of A/H5N1 in domestic animals in Poland following an epizootic in 2023, emphasizing the need for sensitive diagnostic methods. The authors describe an optimized workflow that enables targeted Sanger sequencing of hemagglutinin (H5) and neuraminidase (N1) amplicons, offering a rapid diagnostic approach for subtype confirmation. Their findings suggest that A/H5N1 can be difficult to diagnose even in animals with severe clinical signs. The study's significance lies in its contribution to improving diagnostic capabilities for HPAI H5N1 in mammalian hosts. The evidence is based on observational data from clinical and post-mortem samples, and the study does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

papers.title: From Dietary Proteins to Antiviral Peptides: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Structural Evaluation Against H5N1 Influenza Polymerase
papers.abstract: Food proteins are well-known bioactive peptides, but their inhibitory activities against the influenza H5N1 polymerase have not been widely studied. In this paper, we applied a computational pipeline to predict the antiviral activities of food-derived peptides against the PB1 subunit of H5N1 polymerase. Nineteen proteins from soybean, cow milk, egg, pea, maize, rice, and cowpea were analyzed in terms of their physiochemical properties, allergenicity, and antimicrobial and hemolytic activities, and then digested in silico with pepsin and chymotrypsin. The peptides generated from each digestion process were ranked according to their antiviral activities using four different machine learning algorithms (SVM, Random Forest, IBk, and K-Star) and prioritized on the basis of consensus across multiple models as well as gastrointestinal release and non-hemolytic properties. Peptides chosen were docked to PB1 protein on three independent docking servers (HawkDock, PatchDock, and pyDockWEB) and further analyzed in terms of interaction analysis and MD simulations with 200.4 ns. Some proteins exhibited a high score for antimicrobial activity, such as legumin A (0.970), β-conglycinin α subunit (0.941), and glutelin type-A 1 (0.911). Most proteins were similar to known allergens. The peptides that showed consistent results in terms of antiviral properties and docking include RIQQAIAAGILPLSPL, SSAVSSVCENPILQPY, and QPYRIQQAI-AAGILPL, even though the ranking of their efficacy by both platforms was different. The peptide SSAVSSVCENPILQPY is the most consistent candidate for further research and has 29 close contacts and four hydrogen bonds. In addition, the complex formed between it and PB1 is stable throughout the simulation period. These results allow identifying peptide candidates for further investigation, but all of them are based only on computational results. They need to be proven experimentally.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of food-derived peptides as antiviral agents against H5N1 influenza polymerase. Using a computational pipeline, nineteen proteins from various sources were analyzed for their physiochemical properties, allergenicity, and antimicrobial activity. Peptides were ranked using machine learning algorithms and prioritized based on consensus and non-hemolytic properties. The study identified three peptides with consistent antiviral properties and docking results, with SSAVSSVCENPILQPY being the most promising candidate. The complex formed between this peptide and PB1 was found to be stable during simulations. However, the results are based solely on computational models and require experimental validation to confirm their efficacy. The findings could inform future research into antiviral peptides for H5N1 influenza, but their practical application remains uncertain without further testing.

papers.abstract_zh: 食物蛋白是众所周知的生物活性肽,但其对流感 H5N1 聚合酶的抑制活性尚未得到广泛研究。在本文中,我们应用计算流程来预测食物源肽针对 H5N1 聚合酶 PB1 亚基的 抗病毒药物 活性。对来自大豆、牛奶、鸡蛋、豌豆、玉米、大米和豇豆的 19 种蛋白质进行了理化性质、过敏性、抗菌和溶血活性方面的分析,然后用胃蛋白酶和胰凝乳蛋白酶在计算机中进行消化。使用四种不同的机器学习算法(SVM、随机森林、IBk 和 K-Star)根据 抗病毒药物 活性对每个消化过程生成的肽进行排序,并根据多个模型的共识以及胃肠道释放和非溶血特性进行优先级排序。所选肽在三个独立的对接服务器(HawkDock、PatchDock 和 pyDockWEB)上与 PB1 蛋白对接,并在 200.4 ns 的相互作用分析和 MD 模拟方面进行进一步分析。一些蛋白质表现出高抗菌活性,例如豆球蛋白 A (0.970)、β-伴大豆球蛋白 α 亚基 (0.941) 和 A 型谷蛋白 1 (0.911)。大多数蛋白质与已知的过敏原相似。在 抗病毒药物 特性和对接方面显示一致结果的肽包括 RIQQAIAAGILPLSPL、SSAVSSSVCENPILQPY 和 QPYRIQQAI-AAGILPL,尽管两个平台对它们的功效排名不同。肽 SSAVSSVCENPILQPY 是最适合进一步研究的候选肽,具有 29 个紧密接触点和 4 个氢键。此外,它与PB1之间形成的复合物在整个模拟期间是稳定的。这些结果可以识别候选肽以供进一步研究,但所有这些结果都仅基于计算结果。它们需要通过实验来证明。

papers.full_text: Abstract Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections. Introduction Influenza viruses are respiratory pathogens that pose an epidemic threat to public health. Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are zoonotic RNA viruses whose primary reservoirs are wild aquatic birds1. IAVs cause frequent seasonal and occasional serious outbreaks and have led to four major pandemics so far. Influenza B viruses (IBVs), which co-circulate with IAVs, have no known animal reservoirs but contribute substantially to seasonal epidemics2. Influenza C viruses cause mild human infections, and influenza D is associated with mild respiratory disease in its primary host, cattle1,3. Avian IAVs (AIV) are largely categorized into highly pathogenic AI (HPAI) and low pathogenic AI (LPAI) viruses based on their pathogenicity in infected chickens. Although AIVs do not undergo human-to-human transmission, HPAI strains, H5N1, H5N8, and H7N9, have been responsible for high mortality rates in poultry and, occasionally, in humans4,5,6. The recently circulating 2.3.4.4b clade HPAI H5N1 viruses showed unprecedented spread by infecting diverse non-human mammalian hosts alongside wild birds and poultry. They have acquired a few mutations that confer human adaptive potential, raising the concern of AIVs as future pandemics4. The pairing of the Hemagglutinin (HA) and Neuraminidase (NA) genome segments of influenza determines the emergence of circulating AIVs and their pathogenicity1,6. Pathogenic influenza infections are associated with excessive production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and type I interferons (IFNs) due to uncontrolled activation of host-specific pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), such as the retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptors (RLRs), Toll-like receptors (TLRs), nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptors (NLRs), and Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1)7,8,9. Activation of PRRs by aberrant RNAs produced during severe influenza infections triggers upregulation of IFN expression, which in turn promotes expression of multiple IFN-stimulatory genes (ISGs) that orchestrate diverse cellular functions, including translation, cell death, and inflammation10. While PRR-mediated inflammation and cell death control IAV replication at earlier stages of infection, dysregulated activation of cell death and uncontrolled release of pro-inflammatory cytokines at later stages contribute to respiratory epithelial damage and “cytokine storm”11. The resulting respiratory epithelial necrosis causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and mortality in HPAI-infected individuals3. Recent evidence suggests that molecular differences in innate immune activation pathways determine disease tolerance in hosts. Wild aquatic birds, like mallards, have mechanisms that alleviate IAV-mediated pathogenesis, making them reservoir hosts12,13,14,15. Mallard ducks show robust early innate immune activation during IAV infection, conferring protection against IAV-induced pathology12,13,14. However, susceptible avian hosts such as chickens are unable to mount an early immune response against IAV infection due to the lack of certain immune mediators13,14. These critical variations in the immune responses across different hosts define their viral tolerance and immunopathology outcome. Influenza infection and host-specific pathogenesis Influenza viruses infect the upper respiratory tract (URT) and the lower respiratory tract (LRT) in humans. The URT is enriched in α2,6 sialic acid linkage receptors preferred by human-adapted IAV HA, while the LRT is enriched in α2,3 sialic acid linkage receptors preferred by AIVs. This differential abundance of receptors in the LRT and URT determines viral tropism and disease severity3. Mild influenza infections resulting in the URT are characterized by the production of type I and III IFNs, which enable viral clearance, limiting viral spread to the alveoli-rich LRT3. However, increased viral spread and replication in the LRT during severe influenza infections cause respiratory epithelial damage, leading to diffuse lung epithelial sloughing, alveolar damage, and ARDS3,16,17,18,19. IAV dissemination to the LRT is linked to severe immunopathology due to its distinct immune environment. Alveolar type II epithelial cells and alveolar macrophages are key targets for highly pathogenic IAVs20. Alveolar damage disrupts gas diffusion during infection, exposing the virus to endothelial cells, which, along with macrophages and epithelial cells, produce pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines3,21. Alveolar macrophages, although protective against IAV-induced mortality, can cause lung damage due to excessive cytokine production11. This “cytokine storm” amplifies inflammation, leading to severe immunopathology, morbidity, and mortality. In the bronchioles and alveoli, IAV-induced pathology may cause nearly complete denudation of epithelial lining, generating hemorrhagic exudates in the airway lumen, leading to ARDS3. In ARDS, lung fibroblasts integrate immune responses at the infection-impacted tissue site by responding to damaged epithelial cells and changing the extracellular matrix environment of the lungs to enhance immune responses3,11. Distinct innate immune pathways determine host-specific IAV-induced pathogenesis. For instance, H5N1 and H7N9 infections in domestic gallinaceous birds result in systemic damage and high mortality11. However, wild birds, including aquatic birds, show mild or no symptoms of IAV infections, perhaps due to evolved immune systems. The pathology induced by IAV infection in Galliformes is attributed to HPAI tropism in endothelial cells. However, this is not true for wild birds, where disease pathogenesis is not dependent on endothelial cell infection22. While influenza remains predominantly a respiratory pathogen, H5N1 has been associated with neurological symptoms in humans and mice, possibly entering the brain tissue through the olfactory nerve3,23,24. The recently circulating 2.3.4.4b clade H5N1 viruses show mild conjunctivital symptoms in humans and infect cattle primarily through the mammary glands, which are enriched in α2,3 sialic acid linkages25,26. It has naturally shown infection in cattle, wild terrestrial mammals such as minks, foxes, and sea lions, causing rapid transmission and mortality5. Commonly reported pathophysiology in marine mammals includes respiratory and neurological symptoms, while neurological signs and lethargy are observed in terrestrial mammals6,27. Pigs are often co-infected with both human and avian influenza viruses, allowing genetic reassortment28,29. Pigs show acute respiratory distress in response to IAV infection but generally display low mortality despite mild to severe symptoms29. In addition, ferrets show symptoms of infection in the URT, with similar pathology and mode of transmission as in humans18. In hamster models, IAV generally infects the URT but does not lead to pathological symptoms as in ferrets18. Mice, ferrets, hamsters, and non-human primates are frequently used to study IAV transmission and pathogenesis as they recapitulate IAV-associated respiratory epithelial damage18. Studying IAV infection in reservoir and model hosts shows that the aggravated immunopathology is associated with the dysregulation of innate immune responses. Viral RNA sensing in influenza infection Detection of influenza virus nucleic acids by TLRs, NLRs, and RLRs promotes early innate immune activation, determining the severity of IAV-induced pathology. During IAV infection, TLR3 recognizes double-stranded RNA, and TLR7 detects single-stranded RNA in endosomes, activating nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)-dependent expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines7. TLR7 promotes activation of IFN regulatory factor 7 (IRF7), which further induces type I IFN expression and subsequent Janus Kinase/Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (JAK/STAT1)-mediated antiviral gene expression7,30. Also, TLR7 activation and dimerization lead to the recruitment of the myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), forming the Myddosome complex, which activates tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor-associated factor 6 (TRAF6). TRAF6 ubiquitinates transforming growth factor (TGFβ)-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), stimulating the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and inhibitor of κB kinase (IKK) complex. Furthermore, TLR3 dimerization recruits TIR domain-containing adapter protein, inducing IFNβ (TRIF), and activates TRAF3 and TRAF6 pathways to promote type I IFN responses31. Both TLR7 and TLR3 are important for antiviral signaling and pro-inflammatory response following IAV infection. For instance, Tlr7−/− mice have reduced hyperinflammation in the LRT during H3N2 infection32. Similarly, Tlr3−/− mice show better survival and lower production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines following lethal IAV infection. This indicates that dysregulated TLR3 activation plays an important role in IAV-induced immunopathology7. Treatment with TLR ligands in chickens during H9N2 infection is shown to reduce viral replication and limit transmission, further indicating the antiviral role of TLRs33. PRR-mediated IAV recognition leads to the activation of the NF-κB pathway, which also induces transcription of Il1b and Nlrp334. IAV RNAs trigger NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome assembly through recruitment of apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment (CARD) domain (ASC) and caspase-134. Subsequently, NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated caspase-1 activation initiates proteolytic maturation and release of IL-1β and IL-18. Activated caspase-1 also cleaves the pore-forming gasdermin D, which activates pyroptosis34. When activated early, the NLRP3 inflammasome is protective against infection, as opposed to later activation, which causes inflammation-associated immunopathology35. IAV RNA is also recognized by RLRs such as RIG-I and Z-NA-binding ZBP1. RIG-I is an RNA helicase that recognizes short double-stranded RNA containing 5’-diphosphates or -triphosphates36. Upon IAV recognition, RIG-I undergoes conformational changes to expose its CARD domains to enable ubiquitination by tripartite motif containing 25 (TRIM25) (Fig. 1). Ubiquitinated RIG-I interacts with mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), resulting in the formation of the MAVS signalosome, promoting activation of IRF3/7 and NF-kB to upregulate pro-inflammatory genes9,36. Taken together, these pathways upregulate IFNs, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and ISG expression during IAV infection. Importantly, TLR- and RLR-induced IFN production is critical for ZBP1 production. ZBP1 is an innate immune sensor that recognizes influenza Z-RNAs and host Z-nucleic acids8,37. In the following sections, we extensively discuss the role of these NA sensors in IAV-infection-induced immunopathology. Aberrant RNA generation during IAV replication The IAV genome consists of eight negative-sense viral RNAs (vRNAs), which are transcribed and replicated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRdRp) during infection10. However, the error-prone activity of the vRdRp also produces defective interfering (DI) RNAs, mini viral RNAs (mvRNAs), and small viral RNAs (svRNAs), which serve as ligands for RIG-I activation, which has been comprehensively discussed by Fodor and Velthuis9,10. DI RNAs are formed when the vRdRp dissociates prematurely from the genomic template and reinitiates vRNA synthesis at a downstream site9,10. They are a major byproduct of in-vitro IAV propagation using high multiplicity of infection (MOI) and during extended growth periods38,39. Physiologically, this may reflect in infected patients carrying a high viral load. Dysregulation of replication by vRdRp also leads to the production of mvRNAs and svRNAs9,10,40. Thus, inherent functional defects in the vRdRp appear to promote aberrant IAV RNA production, stimulating innate immune activation. Several host factors, including the host acidic nucleophosphoprotein of 32 kDa (ANP32), also influence vRdRp activity and host restriction during IAV infection10,41,42. Both isoforms of ANP32 (A and B) can bind to the IAV polymerase binding site, supporting vRdRp activity to varying degrees5,41,42,43. Optimal activity of the avian vRdRp in mammalian cells depends on the E627K mutation in PB2, enabling it to bind mammalian ANP32B (Fig. 2)43,44. Conversely, complementary mutations, such as Q591R in the swine-origin 2009 pandemic virus, can also assist PB2-E627 in functioning optimally in mammalian cells10,45. However, the absence of mammalian adaptations in the avian vRdRp may lead to suboptimal interactions with mammalian ANP32 proteins, reducing its efficiency and fidelity. Thus, the error-prone nature of avian vRdRp and its incompatibility with mammalian host factors lead to the production of aberrant IAV RNAs, which trigger RIG-I and ZBP1 activation during infection in mammals. Dysregulated RIG-I and ZBP1 activation leads to aggravated inflammatory response and cell death, determining the clinical outcome of IAV infections9,36,46. Thus, to elucidate the mechanisms of IAV-mediated pathogenesis, it is critical to understand the biology of these sensors. Role of RIG-I in host-specific innate immune outcome IAV genomic vRNAs have triphosphorylated 5’ ends10. Additionally, the 3’ and 5’ termini of the genomic vRNAs are partially complementary, allowing them to form a double helical structure9. In theory, IAV vRNAs consisting of 5’ triphosphates can be sensed by RIG-I (Fig. 1). However, genomic vRNAs bound by the viral polymerase acidic protein (PA), polymerase basic protein 1 (PB1), polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2), and nucleoprotein (NP), are experimentally proven to be poor activators of RIG-I10. In contrast, mvRNAs and DI RNAs can effectively activate RIG-I47,48. While early activation of RIG-I by vRNAs plays an immunoprotective role, its delayed and prolonged activation is a major contributor to immunopathology13,36. Thus, temporal regulation of RIG-I is an important determinant of immunopathology outcome during IAV infection (Fig. 1)13,36. Evolutionarily, host-specific regulation of RIG-I signaling determines disease tolerance and susceptibility to IAV infection. RIG-I is ubiquitously expressed in ducks, particularly mallard ducks, which serve as HPAI reservoirs12,13,14. Notably, HPAI viruses produce high levels of mvRNAs during infection. HPAI infection (particularly H5 viruses) rapidly upregulates RIG-I in ducks, promoting an antiviral state and effectively limiting viral replication to alleviate HPAI virus-mediated pathology (Fig. 1)12,13,14. Moreover, chickens lack RIG-I expression and are highly susceptible to HPAI infections due to inhibition of early IFN responses priming IAV-mediated disease pathogenesis (Fig. 1)12,13,14. In vivo studies indicate that RIG-I-deficient mice exhibit impaired IFN responses and delayed viral clearance following IAV infection49. In contrast, RIG-I-activating oligonucleotide ligands protect mice from lethal challenge with IAV infection50. Notably, certain HPAI viruses may cause severe disease in some ducks, indicating that immune regulation is not exclusively dependent on the presence or absence of RNA sensors such as RIG-I. Host PRRs that sense viral RNAs activate distinct innate immune pathways, which may crosstalk7. In addition to RIG-I, TLRs are also responsible for IAV-induced inflammation. Mice deficient in both RIG-I and TLR7 signaling pathways exhibit increased viral titers upon lethal IAV challenge. Paradoxically, a sublethal dose of IAV infection in these mice led to enhanced viral replication, driven by increased recruitment of monocytes (viral target cells) to the respiratory tract51. This indicates a functional redundancy between RIG-I and TLR7 signaling pathways. Since downstream signaling by type I IFN receptor (IFNAR) is responsible for RIG-I-dependent IFN production, the lack of IFNAR restricts IFN production in mice, leading to enhanced lung immunopathology, morbidity, and mortality during IAV infection52,53,54. Therefore, immune mediators downstream of RIG-I are equally important in determining clinical severity during IAV infection. ZBP1: a possible link to host-specific tissue damage and inflammation ZBP1 recognizes viral Z-RNAs formed during IAV replication and activates multimodal cell death pathways, including receptor-interacting serine/threonine protein kinase 3-mixed lineage kinase-like protein (RIPK3-MLKL) based necroptosis, RIPK3-RIPK1-caspase-8-dependent apoptosis, NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis, and PANoptosis (Fig. 2)39,55,56,57,58. The ZBP1 Zα domain senses IAV Z-RNAs and interacts with RIPK3, caspase-8, and RIPK1, triggering the formation of the PANoptosome signaling complex59,60. The ZBP1-PANoptosome complex also recruits NLRP3, ASC, and caspase-1, thereby activating the NLRP3 inflammasome and driving the release of IL-1 and IL-18 cytokines during IAV infection57. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了有关 禽流感 A 病毒的现有文献,重点关注其与 宿主 免疫系统的相互作用。它研究了先天免疫途径在鸟类和哺乳动物 宿主 中的作用,包括病毒聚合酶相容性和物种特异性 RNA 传感机制的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对 禽流感 病毒 发病机制 背后的分子和免疫学机制的全面分析。这包括检查模式识别受体 (PRR) 的差异激活以及病毒聚合酶在 宿主 特异性 免疫应答 中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,HPAI H5N1 病毒已传播到多种非人类哺乳动物 宿主,并且 TLR3 激活失调与免疫病理学有关。此外,RIG-I 和 TLR7 信号通路缺陷的小鼠在 IAV 感染期间表现出病毒滴度增加和肺部免疫病理学增强。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于理解 禽流感 的 发病机制 具有重要意义,并且可以为严重感染的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 的策略提供信息。他们还强调需要研究 宿主 特定的 免疫应答 以预防未来的流行病。

papers.title: Geospatial evidence of introduction of highly pathogenic avian influenza into dairy farms in the United States
papers.abstract: The emergence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) A/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has led to unprecedented intercontinental spread spread across avian and mammalian species. First confirmed outbreaks in dairy farms happened in the United States in March 2024. This study evaluated the modes of introduction and spread across 42 confirmed dairy farm outbreaks spanning nine states between 10 March and 5 May 2024, through geospatial mapping, case-control ecological exposure analysis, and space-time cluster testing. Non-waterfowl abundance was significantly higher in outbreak counties than in high-cattle-density non-outbreak counties (p<0.00001, r=-0.542), identifying it as a distinguishing ecological feature of early dairy outbreak locations. Knox space-time cluster analysis confirmed non-random transmission dynamics across 14 of 30 threshold combinations, consistent with a single introduction in Texas followed by regional and trade-mediated amplification, with livestock trade, poultry litter, and contaminated milking equipment as likely contributing factors. Proactive surveillance targeting counties with high non-waterfowl abundance and cattle density is essential to reduce the risk of further spillover events.

papers.title_zh: 将 高致病性禽流感 引入美国奶牛场的地理空间证据
papers.source_body_en: The emergence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) A/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has led to unprecedented intercontinental spread spread across avian and mammalian species. First confirmed outbreaks in dairy farms happened in the United States in March 2024. This study evaluated the modes of introduction and spread across 42 confirmed dairy farm outbreaks spanning nine states between 10 March and 5 May 2024, through geospatial mapping, case-control ecological exposure analysis, and space-time cluster testing. Non-waterfowl abundance was significantly higher in outbreak counties than in high-cattle-density non-outbreak counties (p<0.00001, r=-0.542), identifying it as a distinguishing ecological feature of early dairy outbreak locations. Knox space-time cluster analysis confirmed non-random transmission dynamics across 14 of 30 threshold combinations, consistent with a single introduction in Texas followed by regional and trade-mediated amplification, with livestock trade, poultry litter, and contaminated milking equipment as likely contributing factors. Proactive surveillance targeting counties with high non-waterfowl abundance and cattle density is essential to reduce the risk of further spillover events.
papers.abstract_zh: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) A/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b 的出现导致鸟类和哺乳动物物种史无前例的洲际传播。2024 年 3 月,美国奶牛场首次确诊 暴发。本研究通过地理空间测绘、病例对照生态暴露分析和时空聚类测试,评估了 2024 年 3 月 10 日至 5 月 5 日期间跨越 9 个州的 42 个确诊奶牛场 暴发 的引入和传播模式。暴发 县的非水禽丰度显着高于牛密度高的非 暴发 县(p<0.00001,r=-0.542),将其确定为早期奶牛场 暴发 地点的显着生态特征。诺克斯时空聚类分析证实了 30 个阈值组合中 14 个的非随机 传播 动态,与德克萨斯州的一次引入一致,随后是区域和贸易介导的放大,牲畜贸易、家禽垃圾和受污染的挤奶设备是可能的影响因素。积极主动地瞄准非水禽丰度和牛密度较高的县进行 监测 对于降低进一步发生 跨物种溢出 事件的风险至关重要。

papers.title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.abstract: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in enhancing immune responses and establishing a healthy gut microbiome. A literature search was carried out on Google Scholar, Scopus and PubMed using key search terms, such as 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)' and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria for manuscripts used were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms and the examination of viral pathogens commonly found in West African poultry farming systems. This review explores the role of probiotics in mitigating the effects of NDV, AIV and IBV in poultry, focusing on their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. Lactobacillus acidophilus, L. plantarum have shown an interesting promise in countering NDV infections by modulating immunological parameters and enhancing antibody responses. Similarly, these probiotics have exhibited antiviral activity against AIV, promoting immune activation and reducing viral loads. plantarum have emerged as potential adjuvants for IBV vaccines, improving antibody responses and humoural immunity.

papers.title_original: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the use of probiotics to mitigate viral infections in poultry, particularly avian influenza A viruses, by examining their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. The central question is whether probiotics can serve as an effective strategy for reducing the impact of these viruses on poultry health and potentially human health through zoonotic transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a literature search on Google Scholar, Scopus, and PubMed using terms like 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)', and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms, and the examination of viral pathogens common in West African poultry farming systems.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, have shown potential in modulating immunological parameters, enhancing antibody responses, and reducing viral loads against avian influenza A viruses (AIV). These findings suggest that probiotics may be a viable strategy for improving immune defenses against AIV in poultry.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for more targeted studies on probiotics' effects against specific avian influenza subtypes, such as H5N1 and H5N6. There is limited evidence on the long-term efficacy of probiotics in preventing zoonotic transmission of AIV to humans, and further research is required to address these gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize investigating the efficacy of probiotics against specific avian influenza subtypes and their role in preventing zoonotic transmission. Practical applications may include integrating probiotics into poultry farming practices to enhance immune responses and reduce the economic and public health burden of AIV outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the potential of probiotics, particularly Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactobacillus plantarum, in mitigating avian influenza A virus (AIV) infections in poultry. It highlights their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral properties, suggesting they may enhance immune defenses and reduce viral loads. However, the review identifies gaps in understanding the long-term efficacy of probiotics against specific AIV subtypes and their role in zoonotic transmission. The findings support further research into targeted probiotic interventions and their integration into poultry farming practices to improve health outcomes and reduce economic losses associated with AIV outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是通过检查益生菌的免疫调节作用和 抗病毒药物 机制,使用益生菌减轻家禽病毒感染,特别是 禽流感 A 病毒。核心问题是益生菌是否可以作为一种有效策略,通过人畜共患 传播 来减少这些病毒对家禽健康和潜在人类健康的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述使用“益生菌”、“乳杆菌”、“嗜酸菌”、“家禽”、“病毒感染”、“新城疫病毒 (NDV)”等术语和其他相关术语在 Google Scholar、Scopus 和 PubMed 上进行了文献检索。纳入标准基于与家禽益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非家禽养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的检查。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 益生菌,特别是嗜酸乳杆菌和植物乳杆菌,已显示出调节免疫参数、增强抗体反应和减少针对 禽流感 A 病毒 (AIV) 的病毒载量的潜力。这些发现表明,益生菌可能是改善家禽 AIV 免疫防御的可行策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调需要对益生菌针对特定 禽流感 亚型(例如 H5N1 和 H5N6)的作用进行更有针对性的研究。关于益生菌在预防人类 AIV 人畜共患 传播 方面的长期功效的证据有限,需要进一步研究来解决这些差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先研究益生菌对特定 禽流感 亚型的功效及其在预防人畜共患 传播 中的作用。实际应用可能包括将益生菌融入家禽养殖实践中,以增强 免疫应答 并减少 AIV 暴发 的经济和公共卫生负担。

papers.title: Climate Change Impacts to Bald Eagles (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) Within the Great Lakes Region
papers.abstract: The Bald Eagle is one of the most studied birds in North America, and Michigan’s population has been studied extensively since 1961. They have faced many challenges to their survival. From bounty hunting, to egg-shell thinning caused by DDT, to the more recent population loss caused by the outbreak of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, many stressors threaten their population. Bald Eagles are also impacted by the effects of global climate change. Climate change impacts on their populations are not well known, including the impacts of warming temperatures and extreme weather events. Two studies were conducted to determine the extent of these impacts to Michigan’s population of Bald Eagles. The first study examined how Bergmann’s rule–stating that within a species individuals found closer to the poles are larger than those closer to the equator–may be impacted in Bald Eagles with warming temperatures. This study utilized morphometrics data collected from nestlings banded in Michigan from 1999–2025, and from nestlings banded at Voyageurs National Park in Minnesota from 2011–2025 to examine if nestling size has changed over time and with temperature. Additionally, in the event that nestlings are changing in size with time or temperature, we sought to examine the efficacy of the continued use of the footpad method for sex determination in the field. We did so by comparing sex as determined by the footpad and sex as determined by DNA analysis. Analyses of nestling measurements revealed significant decreases over time in many subsets of the population, however very few subsets showed significant changes in measurements with temperature over time, with most showing increases in size and one showing a decrease in size. In many subsets with significant changes in measurements with temperature, there is no significance in change of measurements over time, suggesting some change may be as a result of developmental plasticity and not evolutionary adaptation. Analysis of footpad versus DNA determined sex revealed that the footpad method is still moderately accurate. Continued use of this method in the field should be used with caution, and we should consider the ability to sex individuals using DNA in the future for improved accuracy. The second study examined the impacts to Bald Eagle activity, productivity, and nest tree health from a severe ice storm in the northern lower peninsula of Michigan in March 2025. The storm caused ice to quickly accumulate on natural and man-made structures, leaving over 1,100 km of roads impassable, and damaging over 1.2 million hectares of forest land, including eagle nest trees. Analysis of impacts was achieved via aerial surveys that quantified damage to nesting trees and recorded activity and productivity of known nest sites. An additional goal was to model damage to nest trees not surveyed, and to assess the accuracy of the aerial surveys and model via ground surveys. We found a large decrease in the activity of breeding pairs and productivity of nests within the impacted areas following the storm, with over 50% of the impacted breeding pairs failing to raise young. Even nests without damage to the nest tree experienced failure. Many nests which had young prior to the storm were found empty after, confirming that the storm caused mortality in some nests. Ground-truthing observations indicated that damage to nest trees was underestimated during aerial surveys due to the inability of pilots to see branches directly beneath the nest bowl, highlighting that damage was likely more severe than what was initially observed aerially. The ground surveys also showed that the model was only correct in predicting damage to 40% of the nest trees not surveyed, and that areas not surveyed still received severe damage. These studies demonstrate that Bald Eagles are impacted by climate change, oftentimes negatively, and demonstrate the importance of long-term monitoring of wildlife species. This is increasingly important as climate change impacts grow in magnitude and frequency. Additionally, these studies establish a replicable methodology for raptor population monitoring for Bergmann’s Rule analyses and for population monitoring following acute adverse weather events.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impacts of climate change on Bald Eagles, particularly focusing on how warming temperatures and extreme weather events may affect their population dynamics and survival. The background highlights that Bald Eagles have faced various survival challenges, including historical threats like DDT and recent outbreaks of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Two studies were conducted to assess the impacts of climate change on Michigan’s Bald Eagle population. The first study analyzed morphometrics data from nestlings banded in Michigan from 1999–2025 and from Voyageurs National Park in Minnesota from 2011–2025. The second study evaluated the effects of a severe ice storm in March 2025 on eagle activity, productivity, and nest tree health.
analysis.methods: The first study used morphometrics data and compared sex determination methods via footpad analysis and DNA analysis. The second study employed aerial surveys to quantify damage to nesting trees and recorded activity and productivity of known nest sites. Ground surveys were also conducted to validate aerial survey results and assess the accuracy of a predictive model for unsurveyed nest trees.
analysis.main_results: Analyses of nestling measurements revealed significant decreases over time in many subsets of the population, with very few subsets showing significant changes in measurements with temperature over time. Aerial surveys indicated a large decrease in breeding pair activity and nest productivity in impacted areas, with over 50% of breeding pairs failing to raise young. Ground-truthing showed that damage to nest trees was underestimated during aerial surveys, and the model was only correct in predicting damage to 40% of unsurveyed nest trees.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that climate change may be affecting Bald Eagle populations, with some changes potentially due to developmental plasticity rather than evolutionary adaptation. The studies also demonstrate the importance of accurate monitoring methods, particularly in assessing the full impact of extreme weather events on raptor populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These studies provide critical insights into the effects of climate change on Bald Eagle populations, emphasizing the need for long-term monitoring and improved methodologies for assessing environmental impacts on wildlife. They also highlight the potential for climate-related stressors to influence avian health and reproduction.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on observational data and aerial surveys, which may introduce bias or underestimation of damage. papers.title_zh: 气候变化对五大湖地区秃鹰(Haliaeetus leucocephalus)的影响
papers.source_body_en: The Bald Eagle is one of the most studied birds in North America, and Michigan’s population has been studied extensively since 1961. They have faced many challenges to their survival. From bounty hunting, to egg-shell thinning caused by DDT, to the more recent population loss caused by the outbreak of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, many stressors threaten their population. Bald Eagles are also impacted by the effects of global climate change. Climate change impacts on their populations are not well known, including the impacts of warming temperatures and extreme weather events. Two studies were conducted to determine the extent of these impacts to Michigan’s population of Bald Eagles. The first study examined how Bergmann’s rule–stating that within a species individuals found closer to the poles are larger than those closer to the equator–may be impacted in Bald Eagles with warming temperatures. This study utilized morphometrics data collected from nestlings banded in Michigan from 1999–2025, and from nestlings banded at Voyageurs National Park in Minnesota from 2011–2025 to examine if nestling size has changed over time and with temperature. Additionally, in the event that nestlings are changing in size with time or temperature, we sought to examine the efficacy of the continued use of the footpad method for sex determination in the field. We did so by comparing sex as determined by the footpad and sex as determined by DNA analysis. Analyses of nestling measurements revealed significant decreases over time in many subsets of the population, however very few subsets showed significant changes in measurements with temperature over time, with most showing increases in size and one showing a decrease in size. In many subsets with significant changes in measurements with temperature, there is no significance in change of measurements over time, suggesting some change may be as a result of developmental plasticity and not evolutionary adaptation. Analysis of footpad versus DNA determined sex revealed that the footpad method is still moderately accurate. Continued use of this method in the field should be used with caution, and we should consider the ability to sex individuals using DNA in the future for improved accuracy. The second study examined the impacts to Bald Eagle activity, productivity, and nest tree health from a severe ice storm in the northern lower peninsula of Michigan in March 2025. The storm caused ice to quickly accumulate on natural and man-made structures, leaving over 1,100 km of roads impassable, and damaging over 1.2 million hectares of forest land, including eagle nest trees. Analysis of impacts was achieved via aerial surveys that quantified damage to nesting trees and recorded activity and productivity of known nest sites. An additional goal was to model damage to nest trees not surveyed, and to assess the accuracy of the aerial surveys and model via ground surveys. We found a large decrease in the activity of breeding pairs and productivity of nests within the impacted areas following the storm, with over 50% of the impacted breeding pairs failing to raise young. Even nests without damage to the nest tree experienced failure. Many nests which had young prior to the storm were found empty after, confirming that the storm caused mortality in some nests. Ground-truthing observations indicated that damage to nest trees was underestimated during aerial surveys due to the inability of pilots to see branches directly beneath the nest bowl, highlighting that damage was likely more severe than what was initially observed aerially. The ground surveys also showed that the model was only correct in predicting damage to 40% of the nest trees not surveyed, and that areas not surveyed still received severe damage. These studies demonstrate that Bald Eagles are impacted by climate change, oftentimes negatively, and demonstrate the importance of long-term monitoring of wildlife species. This is increasingly important as climate change impacts grow in magnitude and frequency. Additionally, these studies establish a replicable methodology for raptor population monitoring for Bergmann’s Rule analyses and for population monitoring following acute adverse weather events.
